bull.b: The Dakota Lithium acquisition broadens Dragonfly’s specialty battery portfolio across marine, outdoor recreation, powersports and related markets. Its established brand, customer relationships and prior revenue base could expand distribution and improve operating leverage if product availability is restored.

Early heavy-duty trucking revenue and fleet-pilot conversions provide a potentially durable growth channel beyond the softer RV market. Broader deployments with major fleet customers could diversify demand, increase OEM scale and support higher utilization of Dragonfly’s battery systems.

Lower operating expenses and sequentially improved adjusted EBITDA indicate that cost actions are beginning to reduce the company’s fixed-cost burden. If maintained alongside revenue growth, this rightsizing can improve operating leverage and help move the business toward its profitability target.

bear.b: Persistent negative operating and free cash flow means Dragonfly is not yet self-funding its operations. Continued cash burn can constrain investment in growth, increase dependence on lenders or equity financing, and make execution more vulnerable if losses persist.

Revenue contraction combined with a net loss larger than revenue shows that the current cost structure is not scaling effectively. Stable gross margins have not offset operating losses, leaving profitability dependent on substantial growth and sustained cost reductions that remain unproven.

The Nasdaq notice highlights pressure on Dragonfly’s capital structure and creates uncertainty around continued listing compliance. A prolonged listing problem could reduce access to public equity markets, weaken financing flexibility and complicate efforts to fund operations or strategic growth.
